def-nonnegative-test-supermartingale:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC) [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. Let
$(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\in\mathbb N_0})$ be a discrete filtration
on a measurable space, and let $\mathcal P_0$ be a family of probability laws
on $(\Omega,\mathcal F)$. A real-valued process $E=(E_t)_{t\in\mathbb N_0}$ is
a **nonnegative test supermartingale for $\mathcal P_0$** if, for every
$P\in\mathcal P_0$, it is adapted and integrable under $P$
[[def-filtration-and-filtered-probability-space]]
[[def-martingale-submartingale-and-supermartingale]], satisfies
$P(E_t\ge0)=1$ for every $t$, and has $\mathbb E_P E_0\le1$.

The same process must satisfy the supermartingale condition under every law
in the null family; that is what makes the definition uniform over a composite
null. The initial value may be random and need not be bounded by one
pointwise. Time starts at zero.
thm-villes-inequality:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\mathcal P_0$ be a family of probability laws on a common
discrete filtered measurable space and let $E=(E_t)_{t\ge0}$ be a nonnegative
test supermartingale for $\mathcal P_0$
[[def-nonnegative-test-supermartingale]]. For every $P\in\mathcal P_0$ and
every $\alpha\in(0,1)$,
$$P\!\left(\sup_{t\ge0}E_t\ge\frac1\alpha\right)\le\alpha.$$
thm-mixture-of-null-supermartingales:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $(\Lambda,\mathcal A,\pi)$ be a probability space and let
$\mathcal P_0$ be a family of laws on a common discrete filtered measurable
space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0})$. For each
$\lambda\in\Lambda$, let $E^\lambda=(E_t^\lambda)_{t\ge0}$ be a nonnegative
test supermartingale for $\mathcal P_0$. Suppose that, for every $t$, the map
$(\lambda,\omega)\mapsto E_t^\lambda(\omega)$ is measurable with respect to
$\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal F_t$. Define
$$\overline E_t(\omega)=\int_\Lambda E_t^\lambda(\omega)\,\pi(d\lambda),\qquad \widetilde E_t(\omega)=\begin{cases}\overline E_t(\omega),&\overline E_t(\omega)<\infty,\\0,&\overline E_t(\omega)=\infty.\end{cases}$$
Then $\widetilde E=(\widetilde E_t)_{t\ge0}$ is a nonnegative test
supermartingale for $\mathcal P_0$. The modification on the infinite-integral
set makes a real-valued version common to all null laws.
def-anytime-valid-p-value-process:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal P_0$ be a family of probability laws on a common discrete filtered
probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0})$. A process
$p=(p_t)_{t\ge0}$ is an **anytime-valid p-value process** for $\mathcal P_0$ if
each $p_t$ is $\mathcal F_t$-measurable with values in $[0,1]$ and, for every
$P\in\mathcal P_0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$,
$$P(\exists t\ge0:p_t\le\alpha)\le\alpha.$$

At time $t$, the rejection rule at threshold $\alpha$ is the
$\mathcal F_t$-measurable test function $\varphi_{t,\alpha}
=\mathbf 1_{\{p_t\le\alpha\}}$ in the sense of
[[def-randomized-test]]: the indicator supplies a binary probability kernel by
[[lem-measurable-rejection-function-defines-randomized-test]]. For any stopping time $\tau$, the event
$\{\tau<\infty,\ p_\tau\le\alpha\}$ is contained in the all-times crossing
event, so the definition controls rejection after data-dependent stopping.
thm-anytime-validity:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $E=(E_t)_{t\ge0}$ be a nonnegative test supermartingale
[[def-nonnegative-test-supermartingale]] for a null family $\mathcal P_0$.
Define
$$p_t=\begin{cases}1,&E_t\le0,\\\min(1,1/E_t),&E_t>0.\end{cases}$$
Then $p=(p_t)_{t\ge0}$ is an anytime-valid p-value process for $\mathcal P_0$
[[def-anytime-valid-p-value-process]]. For every $P\in\mathcal P_0$, fixed
$t\ge0$, and $u\in[0,1]$, $P(p_t\le u)\le u$. For every possibly unbounded
stopping time $\tau$ and $u\in[0,1]$,
$$P(\tau<\infty,\ p_\tau\le u)\le u\qquad(P\in\mathcal P_0).$$
def-confidence-sequence:
## Definition

Let $\Theta$ be a parameter set and $(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}$ a family of
probability laws on a common discrete filtered measurable space
$(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0})$
[[def-filtration-and-filtered-probability-space]]. For
$\alpha\in(0,1)$, a **$(1-\alpha)$ confidence sequence** is a sequence of
set-valued rules $C_t(\omega)\subseteq\Theta$ such that, for each fixed
$\theta\in\Theta$, the membership event $\{\theta\in C_t\}$ belongs to
$\mathcal F_t$ for every $t$ and
$$P_\theta(\theta\in C_t\text{ for every }t\ge0)\ge1-\alpha.$$

The coverage is simultaneous over all discrete times. The definition makes no
claim of conditional-on-covariates coverage or validity under a changed
sampling law.
thm-confidence-sequence-by-test-inversio:
## Statement

Assume AC and fix $\alpha\in(0,1)$. Let $\Theta$ be a parameter set,
$(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}$ a family of laws on a common discrete filtered
measurable space, and, for each $\theta\in\Theta$, let
$E^\theta=(E_t^\theta)_{t\ge0}$ be a nonnegative test supermartingale for the
singleton null family $\{P_\theta\}$. Define
$$C_t(\omega)=\{\theta\in\Theta:E_t^\theta(\omega)<1/\alpha\}.$$
Then $(C_t)_{t\ge0}$ is a $(1-\alpha)$ confidence sequence
[[def-confidence-sequence]].

No measurable structure on $\Theta$ or joint measurability across $\theta$ is
needed for this pointwise membership and coverage statement.
